overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated FACTVERSE performance data highlights a clear viewer preference for extreme space scenarios, cosmic 'what-if' formatting, and bizarre planetary extremes. Videos featuring high-stakes hypothetical planetary conditions (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice worlds, and dark exoplanets) coupled with high-curiosity hooks generated the strongest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes/comments), significantly outperforming older, traditional static fact formats.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (829 views) achieved the highest overall views and robust engagement among recent uploads.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on cinematic space 'what-if' scenarios involving extreme physical environments that stimulate high visual imagination and visceral curiosity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal planetary conditions such as TrES-2b ('The Planet Darker Than Coal', 1,031 views), Venus day length (981 views), and supersonic ruby rain (725 views) drove exceptional retention and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form segments focusing on counterintuitive planetary weather, impossible materials, and extreme astrophysical anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content centered around psychological tricks and songs stuck in the head (e.g., 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head', 17 views; 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 5 views) severely underperformed in recent velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological trivia and earworm topics in favor of high-visual-potential science, space, and cinematic narrative concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts with minimal narrative stakes (e.g., simple octopus or jellyfish facts) showed low view velocity compared to high-concept space and earth mystery hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than simple listicle-style biology facts.

next_video.concept: Surviving on a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with no sun, powered entirely by planetary core heat and glowing neon rivers of liquid nitrogen.
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-action falling onto a frozen landscape illuminated only by glowing alien rivers, immediately asking what happens when a world has no star to orbit.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet isn't actually cold on the inside—its core is powered by an unnatural gravitational friction that keeps the subterranean oceans boiling.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' space format and planetary survival hooks that drive top-tier views and high engagement in the channel's current window.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets, burning ice worlds, or TrES-2b
Must focus on a rogue interstellar planet concept not previously covered
Keep pacing tight with continuous visual escalation

experiment: Test a 21-second space survival 'what-if' scenario featuring a rogue interstellar planet against the baseline of standard exoplanet fact videos to measure impact on average view duration and like-to-view ratios.
